אַנְתְּ הוּא עִלָּאָה עַל כָּל עִלָּאִין,
סְתִימָא עַל כָּל סְתִימִין,
לֵית מַחֲשָׁבָה תְּפִיסָא בָּךְ כְּלָל,

וְקָרֵינָן לוֹן עָשָׂר סְפִירָן,
לְאַנְהָגָא בְּהוֹן עָלְמִין סְתִימִין דְּלָא אִתְגַּלְיָן,
וְעָלְמִין דְאִתְגַּלְיָן,
וּבְהוֹן אִתְכַּסִּיאַת מִבְּנֵי נָשָׁא,
וְאַנְתְּ הוּא דְקָשִׁיר לוֹן,
וּמְיַחֵד לוֹן,
וּבְגִין דְּאַנְתְּ מִלְּגָאו,
כָּל מַאן דְּאַפְרִישׁ חַד מִן חַבְרֵיהּ מֵאִלֵּין עֲשַׂר סְפִירָן אִתְחַשִׁיב לֵיהּ כְּאִלּוּ אַפְרִישׁ בָּךְ: וְאִלֵּין עָשָׂר סְפִירָן אִינוּן אַזְלִין כְּסִדְרָן,
חַד אָרִיךְ,
וְחַד קְצִיר,
וְחַד בֵּינוֹנִי,
וְאַנְתְּ הוּא דְּאַנְהִיג לוֹן,
וְלֵית מַאן דְּאַנְהִיג לָךְ,
לֹא לְעֵילָּא וְלֹא לְתַתָּא וְלֹא מִכָּל סִטְרָא,
לְבוּשִׁין תַּקַּנְתְּ לוֹן,

וְכַמָּה גוּפִין תַּקַּנְתְּ לוֹן,
דְּאִתְקְרִיאוּ גּוּפָא לְגַבֵּי לְבוּשִׁין דִּמְכַסִין עֲלֵיהוֹן,
וְאִתְקְרִיאוּ בְּתִקּוּנָא דָּא,
חֶסֶד דְרוֹעָא יְמִינָא,
גְּבוּרָה דְרוֹעָא שְׂמָאלָא,
תִּפְאֶרֶת גּוּפָא,
נֶצַח וְהוֹד תְּרֵין שׁוֹקִין,
יְסוֹד סִיּוּמָא דְּגוּפָא אוֹת בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ,
מַלְכוּת פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינָן לָהּ: חָכְמָה מוֹחָא אִיהִי מַחְשָׁבָה מִלְּגָאו,

he:Weekday Shacharit/Korbanot:1.en: The Sages taught (Menachot 110a): 'This is the law of the sin-offering and this is the law of the guilt-offering.' Whoever occupies himself with the law of the sin-offering is as if he brought a sin-offering, and whoever occupies himself with the law of the guilt-offering is as if he brought a guilt-offering. Therefore, it is not sufficient to merely recite the verses; one must contemplate the reasons for the sacrifices and their laws according to one's understanding.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Korbanot:3.en: Terumat HaDeshen precedes all Temple services; therefore, recite the passage of Terumat HaDeshen before the passage of the Tamid. It may be recited even before daybreak.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Korbanot:5.en: Now recite the passage of the Tamid. If one cannot recite it with the congregation, one may recite it at home and then read it again with the congregation, intending the second time that one is reading from the Torah (Tur). Some require standing while reciting the offerings, since offering a sacrifice is done only while standing (Magen Avraham).

he:Weekday Shacharit/Korbanot:6.en: Some do not recite 'Yehi Ratzon' on Shabbat and Yom Tov.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Korbanot:27.en: They instituted to review the chapter 'Eizehu Mekoman' and the Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael after the passage of the Tamid, so that every person should merit to learn every day from Scripture, Mishnah, and Talmud. For the Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael serves in place of Talmud, as Midrash is like Talmud (Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim 50:1).

he:Weekday Shacharit/Korbanot:28.en: The reason they instituted to review the chapter 'Eizehu Mekoman' is that there is no dispute in that chapter, and it is a clear Mishnah from Moses at Sinai (Beit Yosef).

parts.text: <small>משנה א</small>

אֵיזֶהוּ מְקוֹמָן שֶׁל זְבָחִים קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים שְׁחִיטָתָן בַּצָּפוֹן פָּר וְשָׂעִיר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שְׁחִיטָתָן בַּצָּפוֹן וְקִבּוּל דָּמָן בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת בַּצָּפוֹן וְדָמָן טָעוּן הַזָּיָה עַל בֵּין הַבַּדִּים וְעַל הַפָּרֹֽכֶת וְעַל מִזְבַּח הַזָּהָב מַתָּנָה אַחַת מֵהֶן מְעַכָּֽבֶת: שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ עַל יְסוֹד מַעֲרָבִי שֶׁל מִזְבֵּֽחַ הַחִיצוֹן אִם לֹא נָתַן לֹא עִכֵּב:
<small>משנה ב</small>

פָּרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים וּשְׂעִירִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים שְׁחִיטָתָן בַּצָּפוֹן וְקִבּוּל דָּמָן בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת בַּצָּפוֹן וְדָמָן טָעוּן הַזָּיָה עַל הַפָּרֹֽכֶת וְעַל מִזְבַּח הַזָּהָב מַתָּנָה אַחַת מֵהֶן מְעַכָּֽבֶת: שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ עַל יְסוֹד מַעֲרָבִי שֶׁל מִזְבֵּֽחַ הַחִיצוֹן אִם לֹא נָתַן לֹא עִכֵּב אֵֽלּוּ וָאֵֽלּוּ נִשְׂרָפִין בְּבֵית הַדָּֽשֶׁן:
<small>משנה ג</small>

חַטֹּאת הַצִּבּוּר וְהַיָּחִיד אֵֽלּוּ הֵן חַטֹּאת הַצִּבּוּר שְׂעִירֵי רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים וְשֶׁל מוֹעֲדוֹת שְׁחִיטָתָן בַּצָּפוֹן וְקִבּוּל דָּמָן בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת בַּצָּפוֹן וְדָמָן טָעוּן אַרְבַּע מַתָּנוֹת עַל אַרְבַּע קְרָנוֹת,
כֵּיצַד עָלָה בַכֶּֽבֶשׁ וּפָנָה לַסּוֹבֵב וּבָא לוֹ לְקֶֽרֶן דְּרוֹמִית מִזְרָחִית,
מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית,
צְפוֹנִית מַעֲרָבִית,
מַעֲרָבִית דְּרוֹמִית,
שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ עַל יְסוֹד דְּרוֹמִי וְנֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּ֒לָעִים לְזִכְרֵי כְהֻנָּה בְּכָל מַאֲכָל לְיוֹם וָלַֽיְלָה עַד חֲצוֹת:
<small>משנה ד</small>
הָעוֹלָה קֹֽדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים שְׁחִיטָתָהּ בַּצָּפוֹן וְקִבּוּל דָּמָהּ בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת בַּצָּפוֹן וְדָמָהּ טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע וּטְעוּנָה הֶפְשֵׁט וְנִתּֽוּחַ וְכָלִיל לָאִשִּׁים:
<small>משנה ה</small>
זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵי צִבּוּר וַאֲשָׁמוֹת,
אֵֽלּוּ הֵן אֲשָׁמוֹת אֲשַׁם גְּזֵלוֹת אֲשַׁם מְעִילוֹת אֲשַׁם שִׁפְחָה חֲרוּפָה אֲשַׁם נָזִיר אֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע אָשָׁם תָּלוּי,
שְׁחִיטָתָן בַּצָּפוֹן וְקִבּוּל דָּמָן בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת בַּצָּפוֹן,
וְדָמָן טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע,
וְנֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּ֒לָעִים לְזִכְרֵי כְהֻנָּה בְּכָל מַאֲכָל לְיוֹם וָלַֽיְלָה עַד חֲצוֹת:
<small>משנה ו</small>
הַתּוֹדָה וְאֵיל נָזִיר קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים שְׁחִיטָתָן בְּכָל־מָקוֹם בָּעֲזָרָה וְדָמָן טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע,
וְנֶאֱכָלִין בְּכָל־הָעִיר לְכָל־אָדָם בְּכָל־מַאֲכָל לְיוֹם וָלַֽיְלָה עַד־חֲצוֹת,
הַמּוּרָם מֵהֶם כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶם אֶלָּא שֶׁהַמּוּרָם נֶאֱכָל לַכֹּהֲנִים לִנְשֵׁיהֶם וְלִבְנֵיהֶם וּלְעַבְדֵיהֶם:
<small>משנה ז</small>
שְׁלָמִים קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים שְׁחִיטָתָן בְּכָל מָקוֹם בָּעֲזָרָה וְדָמָן טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע,

וְנֶאֱכָלִין בְּכָל הָעִיר לְכָל אָדָם בְּכָל מַאֲכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַֽיְלָה אֶחָד: הַמּוּרָם מֵהֶם כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶם אֶלָּא שֶׁהַמּוּרָם נֶאֱכָל לַכֹּהֲנִים לִנְשֵׁיהֶם וְלִבְנֵיהֶם וּלְעַבְדֵיהֶם:
<small>משנה ח</small>
הַבְּ֒כוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר וְהַפֶּֽסַח קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים שְׁחִיטָתָן בְּכָל מָקוֹם בָּעֲזָרָה וְדָמָן טָעוּן מַתָּנָה אֶחָת וּבִלְבָד שֶׁיִּתֵּן כְּנֶֽגֶד הַיְסוֹד,
שִׁנָּה בַאֲכִילָתָן הַבְּ֒כוֹר נֶאֱכָל לַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר לְכָל אָדָם,

he:Weekday Shacharit/B'raita d'Rabi Yish.en: The reason we say Kaddish in Aramaic: some say it is so the angels will not be jealous of us for offering such fine praise, and that if they understood it they would accuse us, so it is said in a language they do not know, since they do not know Aramaic. Others explain that it used to be said after the sermon, where unlearned people who knew only Aramaic were present, so the custom is to say it in a language everyone understands.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:1.en: Rabbi Shmuelai taught that one should always arrange his praise of the Holy One before praying. Therefore, they instituted reciting 'Pesukei Dezimrah' (verses of praise) before the Amidah. They established one blessing before them and one after them, which are 'Baruch She'amar' and 'Yishtabach'. One must be careful not to interrupt between them with speech. In some places, the custom is to say 'Hodu la'Adonai' as written in Chronicles, because David established it to be said daily before the Ark. Some add other verses, and each place follows its custom (based on Tur O.C. 51).

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:7.en: This psalm was said by Solomon when he brought the Ark into the Holy of Holies, and he was not answered until he mentioned the merit of David. Since all of Pesukei Dezimrah consists of the verses of King David, this psalm, which reveals his righteousness, was placed first.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:12.en: Baruch She'amar should be said with a melody and pleasantness, for it is a beautiful, pleasing hymn. Sefer HaHechalot writes that it has 87 words, the first letters of which spell 'ketem paz'.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:14.en: Mizmor LeTodah should be said with a melody, since all songs will be nullified in the future except Mizmor LeTodah. It is not said on Shabbat and Yom Tov, or on the days of Pesach, when no thanksgiving offering is brought because of chametz, or on Erev Pesach.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:15.en: A psalm of thanksgiving: Shout for joy to Adonoy, everyone on earth. Serve Adony with joy, come before Him with exultation. Know that Adonoy is God, He has made us, and we are His, His people and the sheep of His pasturing. Enter His gates with thanksgiving, His courtyards with praise. Give thanks to Him, bless His Name for Adonoy is good, His loving kindness is eternal, and to every generation His faithfulness [extends.]

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:16.en: The eighteen verses of Yehi Chevod correspond to the eighteen blessings of the Amidah, which is why they were placed within Pesukei Dezimra.
he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:16.cite: ערוך השולחן, אורח חיים נ, ד

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:18.en: One must concentrate while saying 'Tehillah LeDavid,' for Rabbi Elazar said: whoever says Tehillah LeDavid three times a day is assured of a share in the World to Come. One should concentrate especially on the verse 'Poteach et yadecha,' for the main reason it was established daily is that verse, which mentions God's praise as He watches over and sustains His creatures. It is customary to say 'Ashrei yoshvei veitecha' before it, since we learn from it that one should sit a while before praying; and 'Va'anachnu nevarech Yah' after it.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:20.en: This psalm inspires a person to do repentance and good deeds while alive, while his soul is still within him, and not to trust in human beings who cannot save themselves, for suddenly their spirit will depart from them. Therefore, it is proper to trust in the Holy One, who has the power to fulfill what He wishes to do.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:22.en: This psalm speaks of the future redemption, speedily in our days.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:24.en: In this chapter, the poet began from the great world down to the small world. See the wonders of the Holy One's creation; the upper and lower realms alike stand by His power.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:26.en: This psalm speaks of the future, in the coming of our Messiah.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:28.en: In this psalm there are thirteen 'Hallelu's. This is an allusion to the Thirteen Attributes.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:30.en: These verses were set after 'Kol HaNeshamah' because they are found at the ends of the books of Psalms. They were therefore instituted to complete Pesukei Dezimra.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:32.en: The reason for the custom to say 'Vayevarech David' and the Song of the Sea is that all those fifteen languages of praise arranged in the blessing of Yishtabach are derived, according to the Midrash, from the Song of the Sea and from the verses of 'Vayevarech David' (Avudraham). When one reaches 'Atah Moshel Kol', one should give three coins to charity: two at once and then the third; their secret is hidden (Tzafon Shamir).

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:33.en: During Vayevarech David, stand until 'Atah Hu HaShem HaElokim' inclusive.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Hodu:37.en: They instituted saying 'Vayosha HaShem' and the Song at the Sea as a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt. We repeat the verse 'HaShem yimloch le'olam va'ed' because it ends the song. Whoever says the Song at the Sea joyfully, and imagines himself saved from the sea while Pharaoh and his army drown, has his sins atoned.

consume them like straw.” According to the
Zohar,
it thus refers to the time of the Resurrection,
when God will destroy all the wicked. And with the wind from Your nostrils the waters were heaped up,
flowing water stood erect like a wall;
the deep waters congealed in the heart of the sea.<sup class="footnote-marker">8</sup>
The water became hard as stone and the Egyptians were hurled against it with great force.—Rash i
The enemy (Pharaoh) said: I will pursue [them],
I will overtake [them],
I will divide the spoils;
I will satisfy myself;
I will unsheathe my sword,
my hand will destroy them. You blew with Your wind,
the sea covered them;
they sank like lead in the mighty waters.<sup class="footnote-marker">9</sup>
Seporno
and others interpret the verse to read: “They,
the mighty,
sank like lead in the waters,
” “mighty,
” referring to the Egyptian officers rather than to the waters. Who is like You among the mighty,
Adonoy! who is like You? [You are] adorned in holiness,
awesome in praise,
performing wonders.<sup class="footnote-marker">10</sup>

God is “awesome in praise” for we fear that all our praise will prove inadequate. In truth, it is impossible to praise God fully, and David therefore said (Psalms 65:2) “For You, silence is praise.”—Rashi
You stretched out Your right hand,
the earth swallowed them. You led in Your kindliness,
the people whom You redeemed;
You guided them with Your might to Your holy dwelling place. The peoples heard and trembled,
pangs of fear gripped the inhabitants of Philistia.<sup class="footnote-marker">11</sup>
The Philistines had killed the Ephraimites thirty years earlier when they left Egypt by force. The Philistines were thus gripped with terror when they heard that Israel had escaped from Egypt.—Rashi
Then the chieftains of Edom panicked,
the mighty men of Moab were seized with trembling,
all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.<sup class="footnote-marker">12</sup>

Nations on all sides panicked: The Philistines to the west, the Edomites to the south, the Moabites to the east and the Canaanites to the north. The Philistines feared revenge. The Edomites panicked because they feared that Israel would now seek revenge for what Esau (Edom) had done to Jacob. The Moabites, the descendants of Lot, feared they would be punished because of the dispute between Lot and Abraham (Genesis 13:7). Canaan “melted away” because they realized that Israel was destined to take their land, and their astrologers told them that there was no way out.—Rabbeinu Bachya
Terror and dread fall upon them;
at the greatness of Your arm they were still as stone;
until Your people cross over,
Adonoy,
until [they] cross over,
<sup class="footnote-marker">13</sup>
The two crossings are the respective crossings of the Arnon and the Jordan rivers before entering the Promised Land.—Onkelos
—the people You have acquired. You will bring them and plant them14
Moses here prophesied that he would not be entering the Promised Land, and he therefore prayed that God should bring the Jews into His inheritance.— Rashi
on the mountain of Your inheritance,
the place for Your habitation which You,
Adonoy,
have made;
the Sanctuary,
my Master,
[which] Your hands established.<sup class="footnote-marker">15</sup>
God's “habitat” on earth, the Holy Temple, is a parallel of the Holy Temple on high
Rashi
Adonoy will reign forever and ever.16
This verse is not repeated in Exodus.
But it is repeated in prayer to signify the end of the Ode,
just as the last verse of Psalms 150 is repeated in the prayer whereas it is not repeated in the
Book of Psalms
Avudraham
Adonoy will reign forever and ever. Adonoy! His sovereignty is established forever and to all eternity.17
This verse is a paraphrase of the previous verse as found in Targum Onkelos.
When Pharaoh's horses,
with his chariots,
and his horsemen,
went into the sea,
Adonoy turned back on them the waters of the sea;
and the Children of Israel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea.<sup class="footnote-marker">18</sup>
Exodus 14:30-15:19.
For the kingship is Adonoy's and He rules over nations.<sup class="footnote-marker">19</sup>

Psalms 22:29. The word “king” signifies one whose leadership is accepted freely by all his subjects. Therefore, in reference to Israel who willingly accept the Kingship of God, it says, “For the kingship is Adonoy's.” A “ruler,” however, is one who forcibly rules people, without their consent. Regarding the nations who do not willingly submit to Adonoy's Kingship, the Psalmist says, “And He rules
over nations.”
—Vilna Gaon
And deliverers will go up to Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau,
and the kingdom will be Adonoy's.<sup class="footnote-marker">20</sup>
Ovadyah 1:21.
And Adonoy will be King over the whole earth;
on that day Adonoy will be One and His Name One.<sup class="footnote-marker">21</sup>
Zecharyah 14:9. In the future, God will be recognized by all the nations of the world who will accept Him willingly as their King.

issues.detail: The instruction 'On days when Tachanun is not said' implies the following prayer (h4) is said only when Tachanun IS said. However, the condition for h4 is not explicitly defined in the source. The draft tags h4 as 'prayer' without a 'when' condition. This creates a conflict: if h4 is always said, the instruction is wrong. If h4 is conditional, the condition is missing. The 'when' for h4 should be 'tachanunShacharit'.

See issue on h3. The prayer 'Rabbono shel Olam' (h4) appears to be conditional on Tachanun being said, but lacks a 'when' tag. The instruction (h3) says 'On days when Tachanun is not said, this is not said'. This implies h4 is said ONLY when Tachanun IS said.
